name: rasa.domain.proverbs
description:
RasaOS Domain · Proverbs. The epistemic + longitudinal discipline layer over `rasa.module.research`. It does NOT define its own research structure: the module owns the substrate (one folder per topic under research/<topic-slug>/ — State of play, log, findings, open questions, sources — plus the lifecycle, the INDEX, the three cross-reference layers, and the .claude/research-canon.md seam), and this domain layers on exactly four things the substrate has no equivalent for.

(1) contested.md — claims where sources genuinely DISAGREE, both sides held open with their provenance, indefinitely. The substrate's `Superseded-by:` is the right primitive for CORRECTED claims and the wrong one for UNRESOLVED ones, because it forces a winner at the moment you have least warrant to pick one.

(2) cadence: + last_swept: on the topic frontmatter — the revisit clock. The substrate has a lifecycle but nothing dated: `status: active` says a topic is live, never when it was last actually looked at. Due is computed on read (last_swept + cadence < today), never stored. /sweep advances last_swept and writes a log.md line EVEN ON NO-CHANGE, because otherwise 'checked, still true' and 'nobody has looked at this in two years' are indistinguishable.

(3) research/sources/ — a corpus-wide source registry with stable src-NNNN ids, reliability ratings (a property of the SOURCE, distinct from the substrate's per-finding confidence), and captured excerpts against link rot. It coexists with each topic's local [S1] shelf, which gains the global id as a join key — because the same source routinely bears on several topics and a topic-local id cannot express that two claims rest on the same evidence.

(4) research/timeline/ — the dated axis. A timeline entry is a dated FACT relating N topics and owned by none; log.md records what the researcher did, not what happened.

Additive by construction: a topic carrying this domain's fields is still a valid module.research topic, and a deployment that drops this domain keeps every topic intact and simply stops sweeping. Ships zero subject content.

identity.one_liner: the RasaOS discipline layer over rasa.module.research — contested claims, revisit cadence, a corpus-wide source registry, and a dated timeline axis
identity.subject: research discipline (subject-agnostic)
identity.goal: keep a long-running research corpus honest over years — disagreement held open instead of silently resolved, every topic carrying the date it was last actually checked, evidence traceable across topics through one registry, and what happened kept distinct from what the researcher did

rasa.note: Forked from domain-core v1.3.0. Hybrid shape. v0.2.0 REPLACED the v0.1.0 model: that release defined its own file-per-Subject structure (subjects/<id>.md with Standing/Established/Open questions/Log) which duplicated rasa.module.research's research/<topic-slug>/ folder under different names — the overlap was found after the v0.1.0 ship. v0.2.0 deletes that structure, declares requires.elements[rasa.module.research], and keeps only the four non-overlapping additions. Vocabulary is the module's throughout: topic (not Subject), State of play (not Standing), findings (not Established). v0.1.0 also shipped content/rules/research-rules.md, which COLLIDED with the module's own .claude/research-rules.md on install — renamed to proverbs-rules.md. contract_version stays 1.3.0 per the fleet-wide convention (migrates together at the v1.4.0 lock via bin/lock-sequence, never per-element).

element.description: Files mirrored into the install target per canon ELEMENT_CONTRACT.md §7. This domain installs ALONGSIDE rasa.module.research, never over it: reference content namespaces under .claude/proverbs/, the overlay templates under .claude/proverbs-overlay-template/ (mirroring the module's own .claude/research-topic-template/ convention), and the rules file is proverbs-rules.md — deliberately NOT research-rules.md, which the module owns. The live corpus itself lives under the research root the module's .claude/research-canon.md seam defines (default research/), and is created by the skills, not installed.

files.note: Fork-side guide to what this Element ships and, more importantly, what it deliberately does NOT ship because rasa.module.research already owns it. Authoring-side orientation; the deployment-facing guidance is the framework chapters, which do install.

The stance: what the overlay is for, the division of labour against the substrate, and the tenets that govern the four additions. Installs — the skills enforce this and a deployment needs to be able to read what it is being held to.

Overlay terms only (contested, cadence, last_swept, due, overdue depth, reliability, src-NNNN, timeline entry, saturation, routing) plus an explicit INHERITED table pointing at the substrate's terms (topic, State of play, findings, open questions, the three link layers) rather than redefining them, and the refused-terms table. No field vocabulary — the domain is subject-agnostic.

Five chapters: topic-overlay.md (THE SPINE — the division of labour against rasa.module.research, what the substrate already provides, the four additions, the additive-frontmatter contract, and the rule that the overlay must never make the substrate unreadable without it), provenance.md (the corpus-wide src-NNNN registry, the [S1]-to-global join key, source reliability vs finding confidence, the vanished-page link-rot test), investigation.md (ACTIVE mode over topic folders — question-driven passes, the Superseded-by-vs-contested line, saturation, the anti-fabrication gate), ingestion.md (PASSIVE mode — source-first fan-out to many topics, the new-topic threshold, why ingestion does not advance last_swept), longitudinal.md (cadence + due arithmetic, the clock mapped onto all five substrate lifecycle states, bounded selections, the no-change-is-recorded rule, banded health checks that defer graph checks to /xref, the decay ladder), timeline-axis.md (the dated axis — log.md records the researcher, not the world).

The three artifact templates this domain adds: contested.md (the per-topic file that goes INTO a module.research topic folder alongside its README/log/findings/open-questions/sources), source-record.md (one record in the corpus-wide research/sources/ registry), timeline-entry.md (one dated entry in research/timeline/). Element-owned and refreshed on upgrade, mirroring how the module installs its own topic-template to .claude/research-topic-template/ — the live artifacts are written into the research root by the skills, not here.

Four domain skills, all operating on topics that ALREADY EXIST — opening a topic is the module's /research new, which this domain deliberately does not duplicate (the v0.1.0 /track skill was removed for exactly that reason). investigate (ACTIVE: reads open-questions.md first, registers sources on both the global and local shelves before citing, routes contradictions to contested.md rather than overwriting a finding, stops on saturation, records empty passes). ingest (PASSIVE: source-first, routes each claim to every topic it touches, proposes new topics via /research new rather than scaffolding them). sweep (LONGITUDINAL: advances last_swept and writes a log.md line even on no-change, reports health findings rather than auto-fixing). dossier (READ-ONLY: answers from State of play + open-questions + contested, never by dumping log.md, and surfaces staleness up front). Plus the inherited domain-core Element-mechanics skills — sync, promote, whoami, codify, new-skill, onboard, handoff, resume, update-docs.

proverbs-rules.md — the overlay's gates (contested claims are never silently resolved; last_swept advances on every sweep including no-change; a global src-NNNN is never recycled; reliability is not confidence; timeline entries record what happened, not what the researcher did; the overlay stays additive). Named proverbs-rules.md and NOT research-rules.md on purpose: the module installs .claude/research-rules.md and v0.1.0 of this domain would have overwritten it. On any disagreement the module's file wins for substrate concerns and this one wins for the four additions. Ships alongside the inherited universal rules (contract-rules, output-rules, authoring-rules); rules install flat to .claude/ per the domain-code precedent.

The enforced authoring skeletons (SKILL.md.template, rule.md.template, agent.md.template + README) validated by bin/check-shape. Authoring-time, not install-time; the 'to' target is deliberately outside .claude/ and this must never be flipped to auto-install. Distinct from content/overlay-template/, which DOES install because a deployment authors against those daily.

Subagent scaffold + README conventions. Ships no agents at v0.2.0. A parallel source-triage agent for wide investigation fan-out remains a plausible future addition; until one is authored the entry stays opt-in rather than mirroring an effectively empty directory.

seed.description: One-time files copied at install only. Per canon ELEMENT_CONTRACT.md §7. This domain seeds no research-root files — research/INDEX.md and .claude/research-canon.md are rasa.module.research's to seed, and duplicating them here would race the module's install.

files.note: Per-project Claude session contract. Lives in install-target root; project-owned forever. Placeholder-free BY DESIGN: Element identity (name/version/SHA) lives in .claude/rasa.lock.json, the single live source of truth. A skip-if-exists file is never rewritten, so hardcoding identity here would go stale on the first Element update. Points sessions at /onboard, /resume, and /sync from the starter layer.

Stamped with the Element HEAD commit SHA at init time. Lockfile shape per canon Spec §6 (Connection Contract). Substitutes {{ELEMENT_NAME}}, {{ELEMENT_KIND}}, {{ELEMENT_VERSION}}, {{ELEMENT_REPO}}, {{ELEMENT_BRANCH}}, {{ELEMENT_SHA}}, {{TODAY}} via bin/init's init-only-with-sha handler.

The DEPLOYMENT identity layer (canon SA-025) — project-owned, filled once: what THIS deployment researches and for whom. Skip-if-exists so it's never overwritten. The element-identity layer is the separate .claude/rasa-identity.md, which bin/init GENERATES fresh from rasa.identity on every install; /whoami composes the two.

scaffold.description: Empty directories created at init. The two corpus-wide stores this domain adds are scaffolded empty under the default research root; their templates install separately to .claude/proverbs-overlay-template/. If a deployment moves the research root via the module's .claude/research-canon.md seam, these move with it — the seam is authoritative and these paths are the default, matching how the module itself seeds research/INDEX.md.
